title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Obj. 3: Adam’s binding act does not force Christ’s dying act to restore all
pass_a_gloss: There was not greater force in Adam's sin for binding all humans with the guilt of eternal death than in Christ's death and merit for expiating all, reconciling them to God, and recalling them into the state of grace and salvation: But the very act of Adam sinning bound all humans with guilt and subjected them to Divine wrath: Therefore the very act of Christ dying ought to free all from death, reconcile them to God, and place them back into the state of grace and salvation.
pass_b_english: Adam's sin, they argue, did not have greater force to bind every human being under the guilt of eternal death than Christ's death and merit have to expiate all, reconcile them to God, and call them back into grace and salvation. Yet Adam's very act of sinning did bind everyone with guilt and subject them to divine wrath. Therefore Christ's very act of dying ought to free everyone from death, reconcile them to God, and restore them to the state of grace and salvation.
source_text: Non fuit major vis in peccato Adami ad constringendos omnes homines reatu aeternae mortis, quam in morte ac merito Christi ad omnes expiandos, Deo reconciliandos, & in statum gratiae ac salutis revocandos: Sed ipse actus Adami peccantis constrinxit omnes homines reatu, atque irae Divinae subjecit: Ergo ipse actus Christi morientis debet omnes a morte liberare, Deo reconciliare, atque in statum gratiae & salutis reponere.
